title: Sealed Rooms, Safe Passage
endLine: Sealed rooms keep their own enzymes and conditions, so jobs stay apart.

scenes.tts: The first film showed a sealed room filling with what it could not clear. Walls can trap trouble. They can also keep it away. Your cells make new proteins, and machinery that destroys proteins, in one small space. How does a new protein reach the surface unharmed?
scenes.narration: The first film showed a sealed room filling with what it could not clear. Walls can trap trouble. They can also keep it away. Your cells make new proteins, and machinery that destroys proteins, in one small space. How does a new protein reach the surface unharmed?
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP, carried from the first film (state it in a comment atop scenes.py): BLUE = membrane (every wall, vesicle and room outline), GOLD = GM2 (link-back only), TEAL = the lysosome's digestive enzymes (the same small pair-of-jaws shapes that open and close), GREEN = delivery into the lysosome, PURPLE = small parts, RED = trouble (here also the cytosol's protein-destroying machinery, drawn as a plain RED barrel icon), PINK = acidic interior. NEW in this film: ORANGE = one new protein made for export (a rounded, folded ORANGE ribbon blob, cartoon only, no structure). Labels size 30 or larger, full opacity, at most 5 words, at most 6 things on screen. No molecular structures anywhere. NO title card first, no fade from black. Open on the first film's lysosome exactly as it left it: a large BLUE circle, swollen, with GOLD lozenges stacked in layers inside, tag 'first film' (TEXT 28). On 'trap trouble' the BLUE wall flashes once. On 'keep it away' the GOLD layers fade out, the circle eases back to normal size with its PINK interior and six TEAL jaws opening and closing, and the camera pulls back: the lysosome shrinks to one room at lower right inside a big cell. THE CARRIED WORLD for the whole film, kept in the same places: a large rounded BLUE cell outline filling about 85% of the frame height; at left the rough ER (three stacked, folded BLUE ribbons with small dark dots on their outer surface), labelled 'rough ER' (BLUE 30); at centre the Golgi (four curved BLUE plates), labelled 'Golgi' (BLUE 30); at lower right the lysosome, labelled 'lysosome' (BLUE 30); the open dark space between them is the cytosol. On 'new proteins' an ORANGE blob appears inside the rough ER's folds. On 'machinery that destroys proteins' a RED barrel icon labelled 'protein destroyer' (RED 30) fades in at lower left of the cytosol and drifts slowly there (updater) for the whole film. On the question, a dashed ORANGE path runs from the ORANGE blob to the cell's right edge, and a card at top reads 'Safe to the surface?' (TEXT 36).

Title 'Sealed Rooms, Safe Passage' (TITLE_FONT 54) fades in above the carried cell for 2 s while the question card fades out. The RED barrel keeps drifting; the TEAL jaws keep opening and closing in the lysosome; the dashed ORANGE path fades.

scenes.tts: Follow one protein the cell will export. It is made at the rough E R. Then it rides a conveyor belt of sealed rooms: E R, then Golgi, then the cell surface. Along the way, it never passes through the cell's open workspace.
scenes.caption: Follow one protein the cell will export. It is made at the rough ER. Then it rides a conveyor belt of sealed rooms: ER, then Golgi, then the cell surface. Along the way, it never passes through the cell's open workspace.
scenes.narration: Follow one protein the cell will export. It is made at the rough ER. Then it rides a conveyor belt of sealed rooms: ER, then Golgi, then the cell surface. Along the way, it never passes through the cell's open workspace.
scenes.visual: Same cell. On 'made at the rough E R' the ORANGE blob inside the ER folds pulses; it sits inside a BLUE fold, never in the dark cytosol. On 'conveyor belt' a small BLUE bubble pinches off the ER with the ORANGE blob inside it, glides across the cytosol to the Golgi and merges with the first plate (its outline joins the plate's); the blob steps from plate to plate; a second BLUE bubble pinches off the last plate carrying it and glides toward the right edge of the cell outline, where it stops just short (it fuses in s04). Three chips light in turn along the route as the narrator names them: 'ER', 'Golgi', 'surface' (TEXT 30). On 'never passes through' the dark space between the rooms tints faintly and is labelled 'cytosol: open workspace' (TEXT 30); the ORANGE blob's BLUE outline brightens, showing it is always wrapped in membrane.

scenes.tts: Each room has its own tools. The E R interior has its own folding enzymes, and conditions that favor disulfide bonds. Most sugar chains are added there and in the Golgi. Misfolded proteins are held back. Those that cannot be fixed are pushed out to the cytosol, to be destroyed.
scenes.caption: Each room has its own tools. The ER interior has its own folding enzymes, and conditions that favor disulfide bonds. Most sugar chains are added there and in the Golgi. Misfolded proteins are held back. Those that cannot be fixed are pushed out to the cytosol, to be destroyed.
scenes.narration: Each room has its own tools. The ER interior has its own folding enzymes, and conditions that favor disulfide bonds. Most sugar chains are added there and in the Golgi. Misfolded proteins are held back. Those that cannot be fixed are pushed out to the cytosol, to be destroyed.
scenes.visual: The bubble waiting near the surface holds its place. Camera eases into the rough ER so its folds fill about 65% of the frame height; a NEW ORANGE blob is being made inside, loose and unfolded. On 'folding enzymes' two TEXT-outline cupped shapes labelled 'folding enzymes' (TEXT 30) close around it and it folds into a tidy rounded blob. On 'disulfide bonds' a small bright TEXT clip snaps between two parts of the blob, labelled 'disulfide bond' (TEXT 28); the cupped shapes fade. On 'sugar chains' a short branched chain of small TEXT-outline beads attaches to the blob, labelled 'sugar chain' (TEXT 28). On 'Misfolded proteins' a second, tangled ORANGE blob reaches the ER's exit and a TEXT-outline bar labelled 'held back' (TEXT 28) blocks it; it bounces back. On 'pushed out to the cytosol' the tangled blob is passed through the ER wall into the dark cytosol, the camera eases back out to the whole cell, and the drifting RED barrel takes it in and breaks it into small PURPLE dots, which scatter and fade.

scenes.tts: That destroying machinery waits out in the cytosol. Properly folded cargo never meets it. At the surface, its bubble fuses with the outer membrane and releases the cargo outside. That is how a pancreatic beta cell releases insulin.
scenes.narration: That destroying machinery waits out in the cytosol. Properly folded cargo never meets it. At the surface, its bubble fuses with the outer membrane and releases the cargo outside. That is how a pancreatic beta cell releases insulin.
scenes.visual: Whole cell. On 'waits out in the cytosol' the RED barrel pulses and drifts toward the waiting BLUE bubble; it bumps the bubble's BLUE outline and slides off, never touching the ORANGE blob inside. On 'never meets it' a small GREEN tick appears beside the bubble. On 'fuses with the outer membrane' the bubble reaches the right edge of the cell outline and merges with it (its BLUE outline becomes part of the cell's wall), and the ORANGE blob, with two more like it, spills outside the cell. On 'releases insulin' a chip 'insulin, from beta cells' (ORANGE 30) settles beside the released blobs. Meanwhile the TEAL jaws keep working inside the lysosome.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea. A wall lets each room keep its own enzymes and its own conditions. So the cell decides what reaches each room, what it holds, and how it is kept.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea. A wall lets each room keep its own enzymes and its own conditions. So the cell decides what reaches each room, what it holds, and how it is kept.
scenes.visual: Whole cell, the three rooms in place. On 'each room' the interiors take soft tints in turn: rough ER faint ORANGE, Golgi faint lavender, lysosome PINK; each BLUE outline brightens as its room tints. A label across the top: 'own enzymes, own conditions' (TEXT 32). On 'what reaches each room' a GREEN-outlined BLUE bubble glides from the Golgi and merges with the lysosome. On 'what it holds' the six TEAL jaws pulse together. On 'how it is kept' the PINK interior pulses and a chip 'acidic' (TEXT 30) sits on the lysosome's top edge. The RED barrel keeps drifting in the cytosol, outside every room.

scenes.tts: The lysosome's digestive enzymes are made at the rough E R too, then addressed to the lysosome. Suppose one escapes into the cytosol. Does it work as well out there?
scenes.caption: The lysosome's digestive enzymes are made at the rough ER too, then addressed to the lysosome. Suppose one escapes into the cytosol. Does it work as well out there?
scenes.narration: The lysosome's digestive enzymes are made at the rough ER too, then addressed to the lysosome. Suppose one escapes into the cytosol. Does it work as well out there?
scenes.visual: The room tints fade except the lysosome's PINK. On 'made at the rough E R too' a TEAL jaw rides a BLUE bubble from the ER, through the Golgi plates, and into the lysosome. Camera eases toward the lysosome so it fills about 60% of the frame height, with a strip of dark cytosol to its left. On 'Suppose one escapes' a single TEAL jaw drawn with a dashed outline appears outside the lysosome in the cytosol, beside three small TEXT-outline blobs labelled 'cell's own proteins' (TEXT 28), with a tag 'what if?' (TEXT 28); the lysosome wall itself stays one unbroken BLUE line. On the question a card slides up in the lower third: 'Does it work out here?' (TEXT 36).

Deliberate thinking pause. The card 'Does it work out here?' stays at full opacity. The dashed TEAL jaw waits beside the three blobs, still; inside the lysosome the TEAL jaws keep opening and closing in the PINK interior. Nothing else changes.

scenes.tts: Much less well. These enzymes work best in acid, and poorly at the cytosol's p H. So one that escapes is far less active. Still, a large leak can kill a cell.
scenes.caption: Much less well. These enzymes work best in acid, and poorly at the cytosol's pH. So one that escapes is far less active. Still, a large leak can kill a cell.
scenes.narration: Much less well. These enzymes work best in acid, and poorly at the cytosol's pH. So one that escapes is far less active. Still, a large leak can kill a cell.
scenes.visual: On 'Much less well' the card slides away. Two short vertical bars appear, labelled 'activity, schematic' (TEXT 28): one beside the lysosome's interior, full and TEAL; one beside the escaped jaw, nearly empty. On 'work best in acid' the jaws inside the PINK lysosome snap quickly; on 'poorly at the cytosol's p H' the escaped jaw opens and closes slowly, barely closing on a blob, which stays whole. On 'a large leak' about eight dashed TEAL jaws appear in the cytosol strip, the cytosol tints faintly RED, and a chip 'large leak can kill' (RED 30) appears; then the dashed jaws and the RED tint fade, leaving one escaped jaw.

scenes.tts: That acid is one lock. Inside a lysosome, the p H sits near four point five to five. The cytosol sits near seven point two. Each p H unit is a tenfold step. So the lysosome holds a few hundred times the free hydrogen ion concentration.
scenes.caption: That acid is one lock. Inside a lysosome, the pH sits near 4.5 to 5. The cytosol sits near 7.2. Each pH unit is a tenfold step. So the lysosome holds a few hundred times the free hydrogen ion concentration.
scenes.narration: That acid is one lock. Inside a lysosome, the pH sits near 4.5 to 5. The cytosol sits near 7.2. Each pH unit is a tenfold step. So the lysosome holds a few hundred times the free hydrogen ion concentration.
scenes.visual: The escaped jaw fades. A chip 'lock: acid' (PINK 30) appears on the lysosome. On 'four point five to five' a chip 'pH 4.5 to 5' (PINK 30) sits inside the lysosome; on 'seven point two' a chip 'pH 7.2' (TEXT 30) sits in the cytosol strip. On 'tenfold step' a short ladder appears between the chips: two full rungs tagged 'x10' and a half rung tagged 'about x3' (TEXT 28), for 2.5 pH units. On 'a few hundred times' two equal squares appear side by side below: the cytosol square holds 1 small PINK dot, the lysosome square fills with about 300 small PINK dots, computed from the lesson's figure (10 to the power 7.2 minus 4.7 = 316, 'about 300 times at pH 4.7'), labelled 'about 300 times' (PINK 30). The dots jiggle gently (updater).

scenes.tts: The other lock is the membrane. The enzymes cannot get out. Their targets get in only by routes the cell builds. Two locks guard one dangerous room.
scenes.narration: The other lock is the membrane. The enzymes cannot get out. Their targets get in only by routes the cell builds. Two locks guard one dangerous room.
scenes.visual: The squares, ladder and pH chips fade; 'lock: acid' stays. On 'the membrane' the lysosome's BLUE outline thickens and a chip 'lock: membrane' (BLUE 30) appears. On 'cannot get out' two TEAL jaws drift to the wall, bump it and drift back. On 'routes the cell builds' a GREEN-outlined BLUE bubble carrying three TEXT-outline cargo chips glides in, merges with the lysosome wall, and drops its cargo inside, where TEAL jaws cut it into small PURPLE dots. On 'Two locks' both lock chips pulse together.

scenes.tts: So one cell can build proteins and digest them, without a clash. The new protein rides sealed rooms to the surface. The digesting enzymes stay behind membrane and acid. Walls do more than trap trouble. They decide where each job can happen.
scenes.narration: So one cell can build proteins and digest them, without a clash. The new protein rides sealed rooms to the surface. The digesting enzymes stay behind membrane and acid. Walls do more than trap trouble. They decide where each job can happen.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to the whole carried cell from s00. On 'build proteins' a fresh ORANGE blob appears in the rough ER; on 'digest them' the TEAL jaws pulse in the PINK lysosome. On 'rides sealed rooms' the ORANGE blob repeats its trip in BLUE bubbles, ER to Golgi to surface, and is released outside; the RED barrel drifts past its bubble without touching it. On 'behind membrane and acid' the two lock chips glow on the lysosome. On 'where each job can happen' each room's outline pulses once in turn, rough ER, Golgi, lysosome.

End card over the living cell at 20% opacity (ORANGE blobs riding BLUE bubbles from ER to Golgi to surface, TEAL jaws working in the PINK lysosome, RED barrel drifting in the cytosol). LINE (TITLE_FONT 40): 'Sealed rooms keep their own enzymes and conditions, so jobs stay apart.' Below it: stemhop.com (TEAL).
